Apoplectic

ap-uh-PLEK-tik · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Apoplectic is overcome with extreme anger; furious to the point of losing composure.

The landlord went apoplectic when he discovered the tenants had painted every wall neon green without asking.

Worked Example

When the referee's call cost them the championship, the coach became apoplectic, screaming and slamming his clipboard onto the court.

Apoplectic describes fury so extreme it looks almost like a medical emergency -- red-faced, shaking, sputtering with rage.

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

livid: furiously angry

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unruffled: not upset or disturbed

composed: calm and in control of one's emotions

Where it sits · how completely anger takes over — annoyed → apoplectic → enraged

annoyed vs. apoplectic: Annoyed describes mild irritation, far short of the explosive fury of apoplectic.

enraged vs. apoplectic: Enraged is even more extreme than apoplectic, right at the edge of losing all control.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — apoplec-

Root — apoplec-: a stroke; sudden loss of function from a burst or blocked blood vessel (from Greek apoplexia, apo- 'away' + plessein 'to strike' -- the root of apoplexy)

Suffix — -tic

Suffix — -tic: relating to, characteristic of (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Apoplectic comes from apoplexy, the medical word for a stroke: apoplec- (from Greek apoplexia, 'a striking away') + -tic ('relating to'). Someone so furious they look like they might have a stroke -- red-faced, sputtering, shaking -- is apoplectic.

Use the root in a new word: apoplexy

Use the root in a new word: apoplexy: The elderly man suffered a sudden apoplexy that left the left side of his body temporarily weak.
